title: High Net Worth Property Funding UK Guide
summary: Blog article (not a case study). Per the search tool's summary of the page's opening sections only: the article defines high net worth (HNW) property funding and explains how to access it in the UK. Its thesis is that HNW borrowers often have complex needs that make them unsuitable for traditional mortgages, so tailored products exist that cover international borrowing structures and unusual income profiles. Concrete guidance surfaced: (1) the FCA's current HNW criteria are annual income above GBP 300,000 or assets above GBP 3 million; (2) HNW lenders assess the borrower's wider wealth, including multiple income streams, managed assets and alternative assets, rather than standard affordability; (3) this flexibility allows loan structures that standard mortgages cannot offer; (4) HNW loans are typically GBP 1 million and up. The excerpt cut off before the loan-size section, so the remainder of the article (structures, process, costs, CTAs) was not revealed.
